extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and USPTO staff (examiners); secondary audience: patent practitioners referencing examiner recordkeeping and petition procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and documentation requirements for patent examiners to record searches, claim amendments/cancellations, and to process/handle public use petitions under 37 CFR 1.292. Includes what to record in OACS Search Notes, required search history printout contents, and formal requirements for petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording claim amendments and cancellations
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim is amended in rewritten form under 37 CFR 1.121(c), the original claim number should not be stricken from the Index of Claims but a notation should be made in red ink in the margin to the left of the original claim number, i.e., 'Amend. 1'; if the claim is rewritten a second time, 'Amend. 1' should be changed by striking out '1' and inserting '2' above it. As any claim is canceled, a line in red ink should be drawn through its number. At the time of allowance, the examiner places the final patent claim numbers in the column marked 'Final.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use red ink for amendment notations and cancellations; preserve original claim numbers in index and update amendment count when rewritten multiple times; ensure final claim numbers are placed in the 'Final' column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of Search documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first action on the merits, the examiner must record in the appropriate sections of the OACS 'Search Notes' page the areas in which the search for prior art was made. The examiner must also indicate the date(s) on which the search was conducted and provide his/her initials. In subsequent actions where the search is brought up to date and/or where a further search is made, the examiner must indicate that the search has been updated and/or identify the additional field of search and include the date and the examiner’s initials. Any search updates should include the appropriate databases and the search queries and classifications employed in the original search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly indicate places searched and dates; always include examiner initials; for updates explicitly state that search was updated and list additional areas searched and databases/queries used (see MPEP § 904).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of searches into 'SEARCHED' and 'SEARCH NOTES' boxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches are separated into two categories and listed, as appropriate, in either the 'SEARCHED' box or 'SEARCH NOTES' box of the OACS 'Search Notes' page. Entries in 'SEARCH NOTES' are of equal importance to those placed in 'SEARCHED' and are intended to complete the application file record of areas and/or documents considered by the examiner in his or her search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide which category fits the search performed (complete classification vs. limited/text/manual/etc.) and record accordingly; treat both boxes as equally important for the file record.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'SEARCHED' box - classification search
rubrics_metrics.description: A classification search is defined as a complete search of all the documents in a particular subclass, whether filed by U.S. or IPC classification and it is not limited by any text query or other means. If a classification search was performed, the class and subclass must be recorded in the 'SEARCHED' box section of the OACS 'Search Notes' page along with the date that the search was performed (or updated) and the examiner’s initials. Unless a classification search as defined was performed, it would be improper to merely record the class and subclass in the 'SEARCHED' box without any indication that a limited classification search was performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only record class/subclass here when a full classification search (all docs in subclass) was performed; otherwise do not list class/subclass in 'SEARCHED' without indication of completeness. Examples provided (e.g., 424/270, 224/42.1 F, A61K 9/22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording updated classification searches from parent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When a classification search made in a parent application is updated during the examination of a continuing application, those searches updated, followed by '(updated from parent S.N. ............)' will be recorded. If the parent application has been patented, the patent number 'Pat. N. ............' instead of application number in the above phrase will be recorded. The examiner should recopy the entire search updated from the parent on the file of the continuing application to the extent pertinent to the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit 'updated from parent S.N.' or 'Pat. N.' notation and recopy the relevant parent search into the continuing application's file.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'SEARCH NOTES' box - limited classification search
rubrics_metrics.description: A limited classification search is defined as a search of a patent document classification database limited by a text query or a set of text queries or other means. If a limited classification search was performed, the class and subclass followed by an appropriate annotation must be recorded in the 'SEARCH NOTES' box section of the OACS 'Search Notes' page along with the date that the search was performed (or updated) and the examiner’s initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate limited searches to indicate they were limited (examples: '414/1 (U.S. only)', '238/6 (1954 to date)', '250/13 (cursory)').

rubrics_metrics.name: 'SEARCH NOTES' box - text search only
rubrics_metrics.description: When a text search only was performed in a particular database (no classification or limited classification search was performed), the entry recorded in the 'SEARCH NOTES' box must be: 'See search history printout(s)' along with the date that the search was performed (or updated) and the examiner’s initials. A copy of the search history printout must be included in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not merely list the tool/database name; include the search history printout in the file and record the 'See search history printout(s)' entry with date and initials.

rubrics_metrics.name: STIC/EIC non-patent literature (NPL) searches
rubrics_metrics.description: The staff of the Scientific and Technical Information Center (STIC) provide non-patent literature searches to examiners on request through the Electronic Information Center (EIC). To request a search, the examiner must fill out and submit a search request form and provide as much relevant information as possible. The full text of any citations included in the search will be provided at the examiner’s request. The search conducted by the EIC will include a complete search history. The complete search history in the form of a printout must be included in the application file. The following entry must be recorded in the 'SEARCH NOTES' box section of the OACS 'Search Notes' page: 'See search history printout(s)' along with the date that the search was performed (or updated) and the examiner’s initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the STIC request form, request full text where needed, include the complete search history printout in the file, and record the 'See search history printout(s)' entry with date/initials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations with other examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: A consultation with other examiners to determine if relevant search fields exist in their areas of expertise should be recorded. If the subclass is not searched, record the class and subclass discussed, followed by '(consulted).' This entry may also include the name of the examiner consulted and the art unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record consulted class/subclass and optionally the consulted examiner and art unit (examples: '24/ fasteners (consulted J. Doe A.U. 3501)').

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording manual literature searches (abstracting publications, periodicals, books, other)
rubrics_metrics.description: For manual searches of publications: (1) Abstracting publications—record name of publications, list terms consulted in index, and indicate period covered; (2) Periodicals—list by title, volume, issue, pages and date as appropriate; (3) Books—list by title, author, edition or date, pages as appropriate; (4) Other types of literature—record data as necessary to provide unique identification of material searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient bibliographic detail to uniquely identify the material (examples provided: 'Chem. Abs, Palladium hydride Jan.-June 1975', 'Popular Mechanics, June-Dec. 1974', 'Introduction to Hydraulic Fluids, Roger E. Hatton, 1962'). Cursory/browsing searches may be recorded collectively but detailed searches must be specifically recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording review of art cited in parent/original patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A review of art cited in a parent application or an original patent, as required for continuation/continuation-in-part/divisional/reissue/reexamination proceedings, should be recorded. Record the application number of a parent application that is still pending or abandoned, followed by 'refs. checked' or 'refs. ck’ed.' If not all references have been checked, note exceptions. For a parent now patented, record the patent number followed by 'refs. checked.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly note 'refs. checked' and document any exceptions (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search history printouts – minimum required information
rubrics_metrics.description: Any time an electronic search was performed (i.e., limited classification search, or text search), examiners must include a complete search history in the form of a printout to be placed in the application file. The printout must include the following minimum information: (1) all the search logic or chemical structure or sequence(s) used as a database query; (2) all the name(s) of the file(s) searched and the database service; (3) the date the search was made or updated; and (4) the examiner’s initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include bulky result printouts; ensure the printout documents logic, files, service name, date, and initials. If some elements are missing from a database's history command, add them by handwriting or include further portions of the search transcript (or use log off command where it provides the missing elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence searches stored in SCORE
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding nucleotide and peptide sequence searches, these searches are stored in SCORE (The Supplemental Complex Repository for Examiners), which is part of the permanent file wrapper and satisfies National Archives requirements. The following entry should be recorded in the 'SEARCH NOTES' box: 'See sequence search results in SCORE' along with the date the search was performed and the examiner’s initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not duplicate sequence search results in the file; use the prescribed SCORE entry with date and initials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database service history commands and missing elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Different database services provide different history commands and may omit some required documentation elements (e.g., name of database service, date, file names, search logic). When history commands omit elements, the missing elements must be documented by writing them on the printout or by supplying further portions of the search transcript; in some instances the log off command will supply missing data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the provided table of services and missing elements; where necessary hand-write missing elements (e.g., date for WEST) or include additional transcript sections (e.g., STN, Questel-Orbit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet search engines documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For Internet search engines such as Google®, AltaVista®, and Jux2®, print out the first page and any pages that include names of any WebPages reviewed during the search. Review the printout to determine if the engine name, the search logic, and the date of the search are present. If any of these are missing, write the missing information on the printout. Circle with BLACK INK all WebPages reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use browser print icon or file-print; add missing info by hand; circle reviewed pages in black ink to indicate which search statements' results were actually reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other publicly accessible databases (CD-ROMs, specialized) documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For other types of publicly accessible computer accessed databases (e.g., CD-ROM databases, specialized databases), record data as necessary to provide unique identification of material searched and sufficient information as to the search query or request so that the search can be updated. The record should also document the location of the database and its form (CD-ROM, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide database name/version, form (CD-ROM, etc.), date searched, files and query text; include examples such as citing Entrez CD-ROM with version and search terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of improper minimal entries
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be improper to merely list the tool/data-base (e.g., 'EAST') or to identify the search queries only in the 'SEARCH NOTES' box without providing the required documentation or printouts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide substantive documentation (search logic, files, date, initials) rather than terse tool names; include printouts where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use petition filing formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition for the institution of public use proceedings is filed, it will be entered in the application file if: (A) the petition is accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(j); (B) the petition is served on the applicant in accordance with 37 CFR 1.248, or filed with the Office in duplicate in the event service is not possible; and (C) the petition is submitted prior to the date the application was published or the mailing of a notice of allowance under 37 CFR 1.311, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure fee payment, proper service (or duplicate filing only when service impossible), and timeliness before publication/allowance; duplicates should be submitted only after diligent effort to serve applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use petition content and identification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.292 must be submitted in writing, must specifically identify the application to which the petition is directed by application number or serial number and filing date, and should include a listing of all affidavits or declarations and exhibits relied on. The petition must contain a sufficient description of the subject matter alleged to have been in 'public use' or 'on sale,' including any necessary photographs, drawings, diagrams, exhibits, or flowcharts, to enable the examiner to compare the claimed subject matter to the subject matter alleged to have been in 'public use' or 'on sale.' In addition, the petition and any accompanying papers must either (A) reflect that a copy has been served upon the applicant or applicant’s attorney/agent of record; or (B) be filed with the Office in duplicate in the event service is not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a 'Certificate of Service' when served; include as much identifying information as possible (recommended list includes applicant name, application number, confirmation number, filing date, title of invention, Technology Center art unit number, examiner name, current status/location of application, and 'ATTENTION:' area). Clearly identify the filing as 'PETITION UNDER 37 CFR 1.292' and label exhibits to avoid separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types, standing, and timeliness of public use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two types of public use proceedings: ex parte and inter partes. In the ex parte situation, the petitioner is not entitled as a matter of right to inspect the pending application. In the inter partes situation the pending application is a reissue application and the petitioner participates more fully. Since Feb. 11, 1985, a petition for institution cannot be filed by a party to an interference as to an application involved in the interference except in limited grandfathered cases. A petition must be submitted prior to publication or mailing of notice of allowance; petitions filed after issuance or abandonment will not be considered. A petition submitted prior to publication/allowance but not provided to OPLA prior to issuance/abandonment will be entered but dismissed as moot. A petition filed after final rejection may be considered only if the application has not been published and is still pending when the petition and application are provided to OPLA, although prosecution will not ordinarily be reopened if the alleged public use is merely cumulative of prior art cited in the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File petitions as soon as possible after learning of the application; be aware of restrictions relating to interferences and the Feb. 11, 1985 cutoff; check pendency before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary handling and routing of public use petitions (OPLA review)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition filed under 37 CFR 1.292 should be forwarded to the Office of Patent Legal Administration (OPLA). A member of OPLA will ascertain whether the formal requirements have been fulfilled—whether the petition was filed prior to publication/notice of allowance, whether alleged use/sale occurred more than one year before effective filing date, whether affidavits/declarations/exhibits are present, whether papers filed in duplicate or service has been made, and whether the required fee has been tendered. The application file is ordered and its status ascertained so that appropriate action may be taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure petitions include required documents and fee to avoid dismissal; OPLA will check formalities and application status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of bulky public use papers and public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of a petition will be entered in the file in lieu of the petition itself when the petition and accompanying papers are too bulky to accompany the file. Any public use papers not physically entered in the file will be publicly available whenever the application file wrapper is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing bulky materials, expect a notice entered in the file and that originals will still be publicly available with the file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking and handling 'REISSUE LITIGATION' petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a petition is directed to a reissue application for a patent which is involved in litigation, the outside envelope and the top right-hand portion of the petition should be marked with the words 'REISSUE LITIGATION' preferably in a bright color with a felt point marker. Such petitions should be mailed to 'Mail Stop Petition' or hand-carried to the Customer Service Window to ensure prompt receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark envelopes conspicuously (bright color), consider hand-carrying urgent 'REISSUE LITIGATION' petitions to the USPTO Customer Service Window at the Randolph Building to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted application considerations in public use petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition alleges that subject matter covering both elected claims and nonelected claims is a statutory bar, only that part of the petition drawn to subject matter of the elected claims will be considered. However, if a public use proceeding is ultimately instituted, it will not necessarily be limited to the subject matter of the elected claims but may include the nonelected subject matter. Any evidence adduced on the nonelected subject matter may be used in any subsequently-filed application claiming subject matter without the requirement of a new fee (37 CFR 1.17(j)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that initial consideration focuses on elected claims but instituted proceedings can include broader matter, and evidence may be reused in later applications without another fee.
